classes.name: საქართველოს პარლამენტის არჩევნები
classes.name_en: Parliament of Georgia general elections
classes.finest_note: Electoral precinct: the Code requires the CEC to post each precinct commission's summary protocol (art. 85(4), (8)).
classes.note: Unicameral. Since 2024, 150 members elected by list PR in one nationwide district with a 5% threshold (Constitution Art. 37(2), (6)); earlier parliaments were mixed: party lists plus single-member majoritarian districts with runoffs (120 + 30 in 2020 under the 2011 Code art. 196). The Supreme Council elected on 28 October 1990, the first multiparty vote, is the first convocation. The 2003 list vote was annulled and rerun on 28 March 2004. Art. 37(1) foresees a bicameral parliament (Council of the Republic and Senate) only after jurisdiction is restored over the whole territory.

cadence.locator: https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/30346?publication=36 (Art. 37(2)-(3): four-year term; "Regular parliamentary elections shall be held on the last Saturday of October of the calendar year in which the term of Parliament expires.")
cadence.vacancy_rule: A withdrawn list member is replaced by the next candidate on the party list (Election Code 2025 art. 138).

classes.name_en: Presidential elections by popular vote
classes.finest_note: Electoral precinct: the Code requires the CEC to post each precinct commission's summary protocol (art. 85(4), (8)).
classes.locator: https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/30346?publication=36 (Art. 50 as revised in 2017, which ended the popular vote)
classes.note: Elected by popular vote, two-round majority, in 1991 (President of the Republic of Georgia) and from 1995 to 2018 under the 1995 Constitution (five-year term). The office of President was suspended from 1992 to 1995, when the Chairman of Parliament was Head of State. The 2017 revision moved the election to an Electoral College from 2024. Dates not quoted from a fetched source; first rounds were 26 May 1991, 5 November 1995, 9 April 2000, 4 January 2004, 5 January 2008, 27 October 2013, and 28 October 2018 (runoff 28 November 2018).

dates.quote: Art. 70(1): "The President of Georgia shall be elected through universal, equal, and direct suffrage by secret ballot for a term of five years."

classes.finest_note: One open-ballot vote of the 300-member college; the result is a single tally.
classes.note: A 300-member Electoral College (all members of Parliament, of the supreme representative bodies of Abkhazia and Ajara, and party nominees from the Sakrebulos on CEC quotas) elects the President for five years by open ballot in the House of Parliament; two thirds in the first round, then a runoff of the top two (Constitution Art. 50; Election Code 2025 arts. 111-121). First held 14 December 2024 (not quoted from a fetched source).

cadence.runoff_rule: Two thirds of the college's members in the first round, else a second round between the top two (Constitution Art. 50(4))

classes.name: რეფერენდუმები და პლებისციტები
classes.name_en: Referendums and plebiscites
classes.finest_note: Electoral precinct: the Code requires the CEC to post each precinct commission's summary protocol (art. 85(4), (8)).
classes.note: The President calls a referendum at the request of Parliament, the Government, or 200,000 voters (Constitution Art. 52; Election Code 2025 art. 178); it may not adopt or repeal a law. A plebiscite, called by the Prime Minister, is advisory (art. 180). Held: independence (31 March 1991), reducing Parliament to 150 members (2 November 2003), and the plebiscites on NATO membership and on the date of the parliamentary election (5 January 2008); only 1991 is quoted from a fetched source.

dates.quote: Art. 1(1): "Georgia is an independent, unified and indivisible state as confirmed by the Referendum of 31 March 1991 held in the entire territory of the country"

classes.name: მუნიციპალიტეტის საკრებულოს არჩევნები
classes.name_en: Municipal council (Sakrebulo) elections
classes.finest_note: Electoral precinct: the Code requires the CEC to post each precinct commission's summary protocol (art. 85(4), (8)).
classes.note: Every municipality's Sakrebulo is elected for four years on the first Saturday of October, partly by list PR with a 4% threshold in the municipality and partly in single-member local majoritarian districts (Election Code 2025 arts. 139, 141, 144-157); Tbilisi's 50 members are 25 list and 25 majoritarian (art. 163(4)). Regular elections were held in 2006, 2010, 2014, 2017, 2021, and 2025 (dates not quoted from a fetched source except through the cadence). The 1998 and 2002 councils of the smaller self-governing units are in sakrebulo_1998.

cadence.locator: https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/6720607 (art. 139(1): "The regular elections of a municipality representative body – the Sakrebulo, and of the Mayor ... shall be conducted on the first Saturday in October"; art. 141(1): four-year term)
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of Georgia and the district election commissions
cadence.vacancy_rule: A withdrawn list member is replaced from the party list; a vacant majoritarian seat goes to a by-election (Election Code 2025 arts. 141, 161).

classes.finest_note: Electoral precinct: the Code requires the CEC to post each precinct commission's summary protocol (art. 85(4), (8)).
classes.note: Elected by direct suffrage with the Sakrebulo, with a second round between the top two on the fourth Saturday after (Election Code 2025 arts. 171, 175). The Mayor of Tbilisi has been elected directly since 2010; every municipality's executive (mayor of a self-governing city, gamgebeli of a community) since 2014, all called mayor since 2017.

cadence.runoff_rule: Second round between the top two on the fourth Saturday after the first (art. 175(2))
cadence.administered_by: Central Election Commission of Georgia and the district election commissions
cadence.vacancy_rule: An extraordinary election for the rest of the Sakrebulo's term (art. 176).

classes.name_en: Supreme Council of the Autonomous Republic of Ajara
classes.locator: https://matsne.gov.ge/en/document/view/1557168?publication=101 (art. 7(4): "If general elections and the elections of the Supreme Council of Ajara are held simultaneously, DECs and PECs formed for general elections shall perform the duties of DECs and PECs.")
classes.finest_note: Precinct results for 2012 to 2024 are on the Commission's results sites (sec.ge); 2004 and 2008 are published only as national totals.
classes.note: Elected under the Constitutional Law on the status of Ajara and the Autonomous Republic's own election law, administered by the Supreme Election Commission of Ajara, which is part of the Electoral Administration of Georgia (Election Code 2025 art. 2(q)); since 2008 held with the parliamentary elections. Its members sit in the presidential Electoral College (Constitution Art. 50(3)). Seats and contests read from the Commission's reports of 2012 to 2024 (21 in every election: 15 + 6 in 2012 and 2016, 18 + 3 in 2020, 21 by lists alone in 2024); a contest is the list contest plus each single-member district. 2004 and 2008 dates and seats are not quoted from a fetched source.
